title: Ed Beach's WRVR radio tribute to Cliff and his archive
summary: Ed Beach dedicated a program to Cliff and played his sideman records; the tapes may go to the Institute.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: When Cliff passed, Ed Beach who, you know, was the WRVR --
Yeah, he was the disk jockey at the radio station, when it was a nonprofit station.
That's right. And he dedicated a whole program to the memory of Cliff and I have that on cassette, and he did a lot of research. It seems that Cliff played the piano on a lot of
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
records as a side man and Ed Beach had them and he played all of them and he also mentioned all the musicians who were on the records that he made. So I have that cassette of Cliff's.
Yeah. Ed Beach made, I think, an enormous contribution to raising people's consciousness about jazz.

Oh, I should really think so. I mean I was -- I don't know what happened, you know, I really don't know what happened, why he's not around, but I heard he's out in Washington, State of Washington now.
Either Washington or Oregon, somewhere out west.
Yeah, somewhere out west, but he was really quite something. I used to enjoy listening because he knew -- he had the background on everybody.
These were 2-hour shows and they would be repeated, I think one would come on early in the morning 2 hours and then again in the evening and he would devote it to single artists
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
and in the case of the really prolific artists who maybe a decade of their recording career and they were excellent shows.
And it was their recordings on which they might have appeared, aside from that. And he knew everybody on it. Oh, he was terrific.
That's right. I have a feeling -- I heard somewhere that the Jazz Institute was negotiating to get custody of some of those tapes from the radio station. I don't know if that's true or not.

That would really be great because he really contributed a great deal to the, as you said, the conscience of the jazz community, those who knew and those who didn't know jazz. We have these Black and White albums. As I said, these things came from Charlie Howze's collection and he has some things on this Black and White label, one is --
